tells: 1. Face close is game-era: low-poly jaw/cheek silhouette, plastic waxy skin with a hard terminator, the collar and pearl necklace look like faceted geometry, and the chest hand in the foreground is a blurry flat-shaded paddle (club-4-face.png, centre face and bottom-centre hand)

2. Laugh barely builds over 1 s: frames 12.0-13.0 show the same seated poses, only the white-blouse woman lifts a hand and two heads turn; no shoulder bounce or lean-back, so it reads as a mild glance, not a laugh caused by a line (club-5-strip.png, front table row across all six frames)

3. Back rows are dark, near-identical upright cut-outs standing in a grid, with the silhouette in front of the bar sign reading as a flat card; no seat/table context, they float (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, back half and bar-sign region upper left)

4. Hard faceted silhouettes and flat-shaded low-poly limbs on the near characters: the green hoodie arm on the right edge and the pink jacket sleeve are polygonal with no cloth folds, and hands clamp the candle like mittens (club-6-held.png, right edge green hoodie and centre-left hands on the candle)

5. Aliasing and halo: jaggy edges on bodies against the dark wall, a faint bright fringe around the near heads, a dark smear where the bottom of the frame drops to black, and the empty stage-front black rectangle at the bottom centre of the wide (club-1-wide.png, bottom centre black block and head edges; club-3-mid.png, left-front figure edges)

1. Face close is the weakest shot: low-poly head outline, waxy rubber skin, teeth a single flat slab, the hoop earrings render as sharp jaggy wires, and the people behind are blocky untextured shapes with a cut-off flat-shaded hand floating at left (theatre-4-face.png, centre face, earrings, left-background hand)

2. The wide reads as rows of figures standing, not sitting: the second row's torsos rise above the seat backs at full height and the front row's knees/feet hang off-screen-floor, so the bodies look pinned on seats rather than settled into them (theatre-1-wide.png, rows 1-2 centre)

3. Background stalls are a wall of identical black upright silhouettes in a flat grid that looks like a printed backdrop; no seat rows, no heads turning, a hard cut from lit row to silhouette with no gradual falloff (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-2-mid.png, upper half)

4. Laugh is weak and mostly isolated: in 1 s only the cap man brings hands up and two women open their mouths; the rest sit rigid with hands on knees in the same pose throughout (theatre-5-strip.png, front row, all frames)

5. CG material and edge tells: stretched, smeared jacket textures, a bright sparkle point light in the middle of the dark stalls, aliased seat-back edges and a dark band along the balcony rail cutting the bottom right (theatre-3-mid.png, bottom-left rail and upper-right sparkle; theatre-2-mid.png, centre-right blue sparkle)

1. The held frame is near pixel-identical to the wide (same poses, same head angles), so at the wide the room may read as frozen; nothing visibly differs between the two (openmic-6-held.png vs openmic-1-wide.png, whole frame)

2. The wide crowd is a tight vertical pile of torsos stacked on top of each other with no visible chairs; the front row's legs are long dangling stalks and the green-shirt woman's knees fold through the next person, so the bodies look clipped and floating (openmic-1-wide.png, centre front row and lower half)

3. Face close has heavy artefacts: the hair is a flat, hard-edged textured card with a visible jaggy back edge, the face's flat lighting is waxy, and the woman at right has a broken smeared transparent hand pasted on her chest (openmic-4-face.png, top/right of the hair and right-side hand)

4. The laugh reads as two women chatting to each other, not a room reacting: the men in the strip stay still and look sideways, and the build over 1 s is limited to the two front women (openmic-5-strip.png, centre two women vs the men at left)

5. Lighting/compositing: a flat orange-brown wash with no stage key on faces, the room's back wall is an untextured plane with a lone flat beige card at left and a floating green exit sign, plus a bright blue sparkle in the face close; the back silhouettes are flat cut-outs (openmic-1-wide.png, left wall card and back wall; openmic-4-face.png, left blue sparkle)
